output.risk_summary: You're taking acetaminophen (the ingredient in Tylenol) in three different products at once, which significantly increases your risk of accidental overdose and liver damage.

details.explanation: Both Tylenol Extra Strength and Alka-Seltzer Plus contain acetaminophen. When you take all three products together, you're getting acetaminophen from two sources without realizing it. While your current total (750mg) is well below the daily limit, this combination makes it dangerously easy to exceed safe limits if you take additional doses throughout the day. Taking more than 3000mg in 24 hours can cause serious liver damage, and accidental overdose is one of the most common causes of liver failure requiring hospitalization.

Both DayQuil and Alka-Seltzer Plus contain the same active ingredients: dextromethorphan (cough suppressant), guaifenesin (expectorant to loosen mucus), and phenylephrine (decongestant). Taking both products means you're doubling up on these medications unnecessarily, which increases the risk of side effects like rapid heartbeat, dizziness, nausea, and difficulty sleeping from the decongestant, without providing better relief.

output.what_to_do: Choose only one multi-symptom cold medicine—either DayQuil or Alka-Seltzer Plus, not both. If you need additional pain relief or fever reduction beyond what's in your cold medicine, you can add plain Tylenol, but you must carefully track your total acetaminophen intake. Read every label before taking any dose and write down the amounts and times. Never exceed 3000mg of acetaminophen in 24 hours (that's six Extra Strength Tylenol tablets). A safer approach is to take only the cold medicine for now and see if that provides enough relief, then add plain Tylenol only if needed for breakthrough pain. If you're taking doses every 4-6 hours as directed on cold medicine labels, you could easily exceed safe acetaminophen limits by evening.
